hero.title: Media carousel tile pattern
hero.description: Renders one or more media items as a single tile: a plain box for one item, or an inline carousel with a count badge for several.

i1.label: Dog resting on a porch during a home visit

i2.label: Dog receiving a routine health check

single.title: One item
single.description: A single media item renders as a plain box with no carousel controls and no count badge.

grouped.title: Several items
grouped.description: More than one item gets prev/next controls and a count badge, cycling through the group in place.

contain.title: Uncropped variant (`fit="contain"`, `aspect="portrait"`)
contain.description: `fit="contain"` letterboxes within the aspect box instead of cropping; `aspect` picks the box's shape (`landscape` default, `portrait`, `square`).

standard.title: Standard
items: Use `MediaCarouselTile` any time a card needs to show one or more media items as a single tile — never hand-roll a per-tile embla carousel again.

`media` items use a minimal, consumer-decoupled shape: `{id, kind, src, label, poster?, objectPosition?}`. Callers map their own item type's fields (e.g. `alt`/`title`) to `label` before passing it in.
The tile always renders in a fixed-ratio box (default `aspect="landscape"`); `fit="contain"` letterboxes within it rather than switching to a natural, un-boxed height.
Pass `onPhotoClick` to make photo tiles clickable (e.g. to open a lightbox) — videos are never click-through, since they already have their own controls.
`MediaGallerySection` uses this internally for its opt-in `groupId` grouped-tile mode — see the Media Gallery pattern's "Grouped tiles" example.
Also used directly (outside `MediaGallerySection`) by site-specific card patterns that need the same media box but have their own metadata/layout, e.g. a rescue's field-story feed or honor-roll page.
